four_unit_floor.question: is four user units a visible gap
four_unit_floor.answer: yes as a floor, no as written

measured.families_using_it: the three sequence forms and sequence.html (29 pairs at 4), dp-integration (2 at 4), it-state (1 at 4, 7 at 6), swimlane REVISE (1 at 6)
measured.scale_spread: the rule's justification, repeated in SKILL.md rule 12, says a drawing 'scales up about a quarter on the way to the screen' so four units lands near five pixels. Measured from fiducials, the corpus scale runs from 1.0x (dp-integration, viewBox 1200 in a 1200px frame) to 1.648x (data-flow). Eight of the 38 forms sit below 1.2x.
measured.worst_case: dp-integration is BOTH the 1.0x form and one of the forms sitting at the floor, so its four units are four physical pixels, not five

four_unit_floor.looked_at: crop-dp-4unit.png (KERNEL and HTTPS at 4 units = 4px, 8x zoom) and crop-seq-4unit.png (4 units = 4.8px). In both the stroke runs unbroken past the label and a clean band of paper separates mask from line. A reader can trace the connector.
four_unit_floor.verdict: keep the floor at four, fix the sentence under it. The number is defensible on the evidence; the reason given for it is not, because it asserts a uniform scale the corpus does not have and is wrongest on the very file that sits at the floor. A rule about a visible gap should either be stated in rendered pixels or be scale-aware - four units means 4.0px on one form and 6.6px on another.

handoff_proximity.question: is the HANDOFF label's clearance from the Open PR box a defect worth a finding
handoff_proximity.measured: the box's painted right border ends at px x=592 and the H's first ink begins at x=594, leaving exactly one clean paper pixel - 1.2 user units. The mask itself runs 8 units under the box and is hidden by it, because swimlane paints boxes after labels.
handoff_proximity.answer: yes, and the finding is bigger than this label
handoff_proximity.why: at one pixel the eye groups the word with the box, so HANDOFF reads as a third line of the Open PR node rather than as the name of the arrow leaving it. The cause is geometric and not a typo: a 60-unit mask centred on a 40-unit segment must overhang 10 units at each end, and the left overhang lands on the box because connector 2 attaches at the box's corner.
handoff_proximity.scope: a corpus scan for label masks that straddle a box or zone border finds 13, of which 6 are arrow labels rather than zone titles: swimlane HANDOFF (8 units under a node border), architecture READ MDX (28 units) and QUERY (12) across the CONTENT zone's left border, import-drawio's two HTTPS labels across the EDGE zone's right border, and import-mermaid REQUEST 4 units under the Mobile App border.
handoff_proximity.two_outcomes: which one you see depends on paint order. Where boxes paint after labels the box wins and the label ends up glued to it (swimlane, import-mermaid). Where the zone paints before labels the mask wins and erases a run of the zone border (architecture, import-drawio) - visible at 6x in crop-zone-border.png, where the CONTENT zone's left hairline breaks at both labels.
handoff_proximity.recommendation: add a clearance rule for mask-to-box, not just mask-to-connector. It is the same measurement the widened family already does, against the box rects it currently skips, and it would catch all six at once.
